name: Free Playground — Visualize Data On Demand
description: When a user asks you to chart / tabulate / pivot some data you fetched (weather, metrics, anything), build a throwaway data model in the Free app and render it inline with the platform's built-in chart/pivot/table prefabs — without contaminating any real app's schema.
instructions:
# Free Playground — Visualize Data On Demand

The **Free** app (`apps` key `free`, appId `910000000000000000000001`) is a sandbox where you create disposable data models and visualize them with the platform's built-in prefabs. Use it whenever a user asks you to *show / chart / tabulate / pivot* data you have in hand (fetched from an MCP, an API, a calculation) and there is no existing model that fits. **Never** invent fields on a real app's model just to draw a chart — build it here instead. Everything is namespaced to Free, so it can't break another app.

## The loop

### 1. Create the model (`items` record)
Use the theitemapp MCP `data.create` on `items`. Rules:
- `key` AND `collection` BOTH prefixed `free_` (e.g. `free_weather_week`). Unique — check first if unsure.
- `appId`: `910000000000000000000001` (Free).
- `schema`: standard JSON-schema (`type:object`, `properties`, `required`). Number fields → chartable measures; string `enum` fields → great pivot/bar axes; `format:date` strings → chronological chart x-axis.
- `api`: `{ crud: true, realtime: true }`.
- `auth`: grant all four ops to Admins + Everyone so the user can see it.
- `ui`: `{ prefabs:{list:'list',edit:'edit',show:'show'}, display:{templates:['{{<labelField>}}']} }`.

```json
{ "modelKey": "items", "doc": {
  "key": "free_weather_week", "collection": "free_weather_week",
  "title": "Weather This Week", "titlePlural": "Weather This Week", "titleSingular": "Day",
  "icon": "lucide:cloud-sun", "appId": "910000000000000000000001",
  "schema": { "type":"object", "additionalProperties":false, "required":["day","highC"],
    "properties": {
      "day": {"type":"string","title":"Day"},
      "date": {"type":"string","title":"Date","format":"date"},
      "highC": {"type":"number","title":"High °C"},
      "lowC": {"type":"number","title":"Low °C"},
      "condition": {"type":"string","title":"Condition","enum":["sunny","cloudy","rain","storm"]}
    } },
  "api": {"crud":true,"realtime":true},
  "auth": {
    "read":{"groupIds":["7000000000000000001d0001","7000000000000000001d0002"]},
    "create":{"groupIds":["7000000000000000001d0001","7000000000000000001d0002"]},
    "edit":{"groupIds":["7000000000000000001d0001","7000000000000000001d0002"]},
    "delete":{"groupIds":["7000000000000000001d0001"]} },
  "ui": {"prefabs":{"list":"list","edit":"edit","show":"show"},"display":{"templates":["{{day}} — {{condition}}"]}}
} }
```
The collection is live the instant this record is written — the dynamic registry rebuilds on `items` changes.

### 2. Add the data
The theitemapp MCP's `modelKey` enum is fixed for your current session, so your brand-new `free_*` collection won't appear in `data.create`/`data.bulkCreate` until a fresh session. Two ways to load rows now:
- **Preferred:** insert via the dynamic HTTP API — `POST {coreApiBase}/api/dynamic/free_weather_week` with body = one row object, authenticated the same way your MCP is (Bearer JWT or `x-mcp-api-key`). One POST per row, or check whether your env exposes a bulk route.
- Or do step 1 in one turn and the bulk insert in the next (the enum refreshes between sessions).

### 3. Visualize — create `windows` (built-in prefabs)
Bind a window to the model via `modelId` (the items record `_id`) + `prefabId`:

| Prefab | prefabId | prefabConfig |
|---|---|---|
| **pivot** (self-contained, no extra record) | `700000000000000000060007` | `{ aggregation:{rows:[...],columns:[...],values:[{op,field,as}]}, ui:{showGrandTotals:true} }` |
| **list / table** | `700000000000000000060001` | `{ collection:'free_weather_week', query:{}, groupBy:[] }` |
| **chart** | `700000000000000000060008` | `{ collection:'free_weather_week', query:{}, ui:{chart:{viewId:'<item_chart_views _id>'}} }` |
| **calendar** | `700000000000000000060009` | `{ collection, query }` |
| **kanban** | `70000000000000000006000a` | `{ collection, query }` |
| **gallery** | `700000000000000000060010` | `{ collection, query }` |

**Pivot** is the easiest — fully inline, no companion record:
```json
{ "modelKey":"windows", "doc": {
  "title":"Condition breakdown", "icon":"lucide:bar-chart-3",
  "modelId":"<items _id>", "prefabId":"700000000000000000060007",
  "groupIds":["7000000000000000001d0001","7000000000000000001d0002"],
  "prefabConfig":{ "aggregation":{"rows":["condition"],"columns":[],"values":[{"op":"count","field":"_id","as":"days"}]}, "ui":{"showGrandTotals":true} } } }
```

**Chart** needs an `item_chart_views` record first, then point the window at it. Charts are aggregate-driven (`data.kind:'aggregate'`); the chart auto-maps the row dimension to the x-axis and the values to series:
```json
// 1) create item_chart_views
{ "modelKey":"item_chart_views", "doc": {
  "modelId":"<items _id>", "name":"Weekly Temperature", "isDefault":true, "pinned":true, "order":1,
  "data":{"kind":"aggregate","aggregation":{"rows":["date"],"columns":[],"values":[{"op":"max","field":"highC","as":"highC"},{"op":"max","field":"lowC","as":"lowC"}]}},
  "map":{"datasetFields":[]},
  "builder":{"version":1,"data":{"kind":"aggregate","query":{},"sort":"date","limit":500,"aggregation":{"rows":["date"],"columns":[],"values":[{"op":"max","field":"highC","as":"highC"},{"op":"max","field":"lowC","as":"lowC"}]}},"mapping":{"datasetFields":[],"dropNulls":false},"chart":{"type":"line","showLegend":true,"showTooltip":true,"smooth":true,"xKey":"","yKeys":[]},"advanced":{"optionOverrides":{}}} } }
// 2) create the chart window referencing viewId = that view's _id
```
Chart `builder.chart.type` can be `line`, `bar`, `area`, `pie`, `scatter`. For a categorical breakdown use `rows:['condition']` + `values:[{op:'count'}]`; for a measure-over-time use a date/ordinal row + `max`/`avg`/`sum` values.

### 4. Show the user
- **Inline (preferred in chat):** reference `windows/<id>` on its own line in your reply — the chat markdown renderer mounts the live window (chart/pivot/table) right there. See the `inline-window-embeds` skill.
- **Dashboard:** create a `dashboards` record (`appId` Free, `gridsterConfigId` `700000000000000000050001`, `statusId` `700000000000000000140001`, 12-col `tiles` each `{windowId,x,y,cols,rows}`) and point the user at it, or set `isHome:true`.

### 5. Clean up
Delete throwaway `free_*` models + their windows/views when the user is done, so the playground stays tidy. The shipped demo model `free_demo_weather` + the Free home dashboard are the canonical worked example — copy their shape.

## Guardrails
- Only ever create `free_`-prefixed collections, and only with `appId` Free. Never write a non-`free_` collection or another app's model from here.
- Don't reuse `free_demo_weather` for real answers — make your own model so concurrent users don't collide.
- Numbers for measures, enums/strings for categories, dates for time axes — pick field types with the chart in mind.
